reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: “Taylor” (David Jonsson) has been told that early release might be in the offing if he can keep his nose clean for a few more weeks in prison. He generally keeps himself to himself, and offers the floor’s drug pedlars a short back and sides now and again in return for a supply of pills. When the newly arrived “Dee” (Tom Blyth) is put into his cell, the pair quickly seem to strike up a sort of friendship as the enterprising newbie sets up a shop trading everything from chocolate to drugs. Needless to say, the established traders don’t take kindly to his new business and so set about restoring their preferred equilibrium. Whilst that might work for them, though, it puts a great and perilous strain on “Taylor” whose chances of parole could well be compromised by the behaviour of his now very angry and vengeful cell-mate. This is a quickly paced and authentic looking prison drama that shows us a dog-eat-dog world at it’s most violent. The prison officers are plentiful enough but seem incapable of stemming the regular drone deliveries or of stopping the gang warfare that prevails amongst inmates for whom law and order is defined more by a survival of the fittest mentality. Jonsson offers us a calm and measured character who is understated and ostensibly just biding his time til he can rejoin his son; Blyth on the other hand presents a much more blatantly aggressive and manipulative character and Cal McCau manages to blend the two together convincingly as this story heads towards a denouement that I felt clever, unexpected and really quite fitting. It’s one of those films that showcases jail as little more than a zoo for society’s undesirables, but this time there is a man with some semblance of integrity and shrewdness behind the bars who is playing a game of his own - and it’s well worth ninety minutes.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Fresh out on parole, Taylor's hopes for a clean slate are threatened when he is paired with an unpredictable cellmate whose loyalties force him to make a deadly choice.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: After serving time, Taylor is determined to rebuild his life upon being granted parole. However, his path to redemption is derailed by the arrival of Dee, an intense cellmate who quickly takes Taylor under his wing. When a vicious attack suddenly escalates tensions, Taylor finds himself caught between his loyalty to Dee and his hard-earned chance at freedom.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Taylor enters his parole period with a singular focus: leave his troubled past behind and start fresh. His plan for a quiet transition is disrupted when he is paired with Dee, a charismatic yet volatile cellmate who takes Taylor under his wing. As Dee pulls Taylor deeper into his orbit, the line between mentorship and dangerous influence begins to blur. Outside and inside the prison walls, old grudges resurface, culminating in a brutal attack that leaves both men reeling. In the chaotic aftermath, Taylor is forced to navigate a precarious web of loyalty, fear, and survival. Dee demands solidarity, but following him means risking the very freedom Taylor fought so hard to reclaim. As pressure mounts from both sides of the law, Taylor must decide how much he is willing to sacrifice for a brother in arms. Ultimately, Taylor reaches a violent turning point where protecting Dee could mean permanently destroying his own future.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Wasteman is a tense crime thriller that follows Taylor, a man attempting to navigate the precarious waters of life post-parole. Eager to turn over a new leaf and distance himself from a criminal past, Taylor's path takes an unexpected turn when he crosses paths with Dee, a domineering cellmate who quickly integrates himself into Taylor's life. As Dee assumes the role of a mentor, Taylor is drawn into an unstable dynamic where loyalty is tested by escalating violence. When a sudden attack jeopardizes their standing, Taylor is confronted with a brutal dilemma: stand by the man who took him under his wing, or protect his own fragile second chance at freedom.
